projectBackground.name: Hospital HVAC Retrofit — Outpatient Wing
projectBackground.context: The outpatient wing is too warm and under-ventilated. The retrofit must meet ventilation rates without oversizing.

manager.name: Dieter Hartmann
manager.role: Head of Building Services, Hartmann Process Engineering
manager.note: Oversized plant is not safe plant; it short-cycles and wastes energy. Size it from the load, not from habit.

assignment.title: Size the retrofit from first principles
assignment.brief: Calculate cooling, ventilation and chiller efficiency, complete a room schedule in Excel and justify the sizing.

documents.name: Room Data
documents.note: Room volume 600 m³; 50 occupants at 10 L/s each.

documents.name: Airflow Data
documents.note: Supply airflow 2 m³/s; supply-room temperature difference 10 K.

documents.name: Chiller Data
documents.note: Cooling output 300 kW; electrical input 75 kW.

tasks.title: Ventilation Airflow
tasks.prompt: 50 occupants at 10 L/s each. What is the required airflow in m³/s?
tasks.tip: Check the code rate per person.
tasks.mistake: Mixing L/s and m³/s causes 1,000x errors.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Air Changes
tasks.prompt: A room of 600 m³ receives 0.5 m³/s. How many air changes per hour (ACH)?
tasks.tip: Compare to guidance for the room type.
tasks.mistake: Forgetting to convert seconds to hours gives 0.05 ACH.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Sensible Cooling
tasks.prompt: Cooling = 1.2 x 1.005 x airflow (m³/s) x ΔT. Airflow 2 m³/s, ΔT 10 K. What is it (kW)?
tasks.reasoning: Sensible load depends on airflow and temperature difference.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Chiller COP
tasks.prompt: Cooling output 300 kW, electrical input 75 kW. What is the COP?
tasks.mistake: Quoting peak COP overstates seasonal efficiency.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Room Schedule (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Cooling in kW (D = 1.2 x 1.005 x B x C) per room. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: A room schedule sums to the plant size.
tasks.mistake: Adding a safety factor on every room multiplies oversizing.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Sizing Justification
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence justification for not oversizing the chiller.
tasks.modelAnswer: The waiting hall needs 24 kW of sensible cooling and the three rooms total about 41 kW, so a modest chiller with part-load capability meets the load. Oversizing causes short-cycling, poorer humidity control and higher energy use at typical part loads. I recommend a modular chiller with a COP of 4.0 or better and variable-speed fans so efficiency holds throughout the year. Future expansion can be added as modules.
tasks.reasoning: A good justification links the load to the sizing and the operational consequence.
tasks.mistake: Adding margin blindly is not engineering.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Oversized Chiller
caseStudy.background: A hospital installed a chiller 50% larger than needed 'to be safe'. It cycled constantly, humidity rose and the energy bill was 30% above forecast.
caseStudy.challenges: Safety margins were added at every step.
questions: Why did the extra capacity hurt?
caseStudy.solution: Hartmann adopted load calculations with a single documented margin and part-load performance checks.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Right-size; extra margin has a cost.

prompts: Where would you add margin and why?
How do you check the system at part load?
